title: spec(types,react,core): every node slot is SchemaNode (= BaseSchema), so after objectui#8347's removal an inline child carrying its own type's keys stops compiling; type node slots and SchemaRenderer's schema prop as the declared node union
body:
Blocked-by: #11543

This card carries objectui#8347's **F1** half: the TypeScript type of a node slot and of `SchemaRenderer`'s `schema` prop. objectui#8347 keeps the removal itself and everything its fork ACCEPT lists for the last PR.

Filing-gate category: ① — a named landing point (`SchemaNode` in `@object-ui/types`, `SchemaRenderer`'s `schema` prop in `@object-ui/react`, `@object-ui/core`'s schema builder), measured reach, and named producers, ordered by the objectui#7927 ruling's step 1. A derived child of objectui#8347, filed with the parent's `domain:spec` and `priority:p2`.
Reader: the `domain:spec @ objectui` seat (objectui#10217) dispatches it, and an os-dev executes it.
Parent: objectui#8347, which is `pm:blocked` until this card and its two siblings land.

## What was measured (objectui#8347's P1 report `5953663875`, at `main` `5988b6b53`)

`SchemaNode` is `BaseSchema | string | number | boolean | null | undefined` (`packages/types/src/base.ts`, read on `origin/main`), and every node slot (`children`, `trigger`, `content`, a view's `schema`) uses it. `SchemaRenderer`'s `schema` prop is `BaseSchema | AuthoringNode | string | null | undefined`. With `BaseSchema`'s index signature deleted alone:

- an inline child that carries its own type's keys (a text node's `content`, a statistic's `value`, a button's `variant`) stops compiling, and per-child `satisfies TextSchema` does not help, because the slot still excess-checks the literal against `BaseSchema` (measured by a type probe);
- **8 test and example literals:** types `page-body-arity-8310` ×3, `overlay-trigger-union-7081` ×2, `@object-ui/core`'s schema builder ×2 (`.child()` takes `BaseSchema`), and the types example's `HeaderBarSchema` cast ×1;
- **17 doc diagnostics** in `check:doc-snippets`: `schema-renderer.mdx` ×3 (including a custom widget's `customProp`), `architecture.md`, `quick-start.md`, `schema-playground.md`, `schema-rendering.md`, `enhanced-actions.mdx`, `building-crud-app.md` and `data-source.md` (`objectName` on a detail node), the `objectos-integration.mdx` page template, the plugin-detail README ×3, the plugin-view README ×2, and the types README's crumbs;
- `check:doc-examples`: `SchemaNode`'s own docblock example (`content` on a `BaseSchema` literal).

`reach:` the published `SchemaNode` type and the `SchemaRenderer` prop. The named producers are the getting-started docs above and `@object-ui/core`'s `.child()`. Today they compile only through the index signature.

## Seat ruling: A, conditioned on a premise (inside the maintainer's veto window)

**Governing text:** the objectui#5250 ruling as objectui#8347's body quotes it: "the TypeScript side gets the matching authoring types without the `[key: string]: any` index signature ... so an invented or misspelled key is distinguishable from a declared one at the authoring site". A nested child is an authoring site.

- **① The ruling:** node slots (the object arm of `SchemaNode`) and `SchemaRenderer`'s `schema` prop take the discriminated union of the declared node types, keyed by `type` (`AnySchema` ∪ `AuthoringNode`).
  - Option B (keep `BaseSchema` and make every nested node a pre-typed constant) pushes TypeScript authors to `as` casts at the authoring site, which is tolerance where the error should be refused.
  - Option C (an explicit open record for children only) re-creates the index signature one level down, which the objectui#7927 removal ruling refuses.
- **② The premise, which the implementer measures first, before any other edit.** Under objectui#8347's P1 mutation (the six `BaseSchema` lines deleted alone), with a throwaway probe file compiled by `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`:
  - (a) an inline child of a declared type with a misspelled key is REFUSED, and the correctly spelled control compiles, both at a nested slot and at the `SchemaRenderer` prop;
  - (b) a node of a registered custom type (the `schema-renderer.mdx` custom widget is the named instance) stays authorable through a mechanism that does NOT let a declared type's literal escape its own arm's excess check;
  - (c) the type-check time of the `types`, `react` and `components` programs is reported before and after, as a number. That is evidence for the seat, not a stop condition.
- **③ The prohibition:** if (a) or (b) fails, report the fork with the probe evidence. ⛔ Do not fall back silently to B or C, ⛔ do not add an index signature or a `type: string` catch-all arm at the slot, and ⛔ do not grow the card.

## Constraints

- Every edit here must compile WITH the signature still present, so this card lands on its own and `main` stays green. The removal stays objectui#8347's.
- The listed tests and docs move with the type: a doc block whose example now fails compiles against the new slot type, or is re-annotated with the declared node type.
- The compile-fail pin rides here: a misspelled key on a nested child is refused under the P1 mutation (assert it with the mutation applied in a probe, or with a test that declares the stripped shape locally). The correct spelling still compiles.
- `Clause-②` is stated at claim from the actual accept-set change. With the signature present, a member union of index-signature types accepts what `BaseSchema` accepts today.

## Dedupe

REST list of objectui's 600 most recently updated issues and PRs, open and closed (back to 2026-09-28T12:31Z), grepped locally on 2026-10-02: `SchemaNode` 13 hits, all closed PRs or the closed preparation card objectui#11364; "node slot / nested child type" 6 hits, none open on this question (objectui#11069 is the `validate` wiring); control `objectui` 589.

Dedupe words: `SchemaNode slot union` · `inline child excess property BaseSchema` · `SchemaRenderer schema prop node union`
